steps.title: Prepare pCAG‑GFP empty vector
steps.instruction: Construct a pCAG‑GFP vector containing a miRNA frame sequence (pCAG‑GFP empty vector) using the BLOCK‑iT Pol II miR kit and standard cloning reagents.

substeps.instruction: Subclone the miR frame sequence from pcDNA™6.2‑GW/EmGFP‑miR (BLOCK‑iT kit) with primers forward 5’-AAAGCGGCCGCCCTGGAGGCTTGCTGAAGG-3’ and reverse 5’-AGTGCGGCCGCGGCCATTTGTTCCATGTGA-3’ using the same PCR protocol as cDNA subcloning (Protocol 25‑34, steps 1‑2).
Linearize 1 µL pCAG‑GFP (Addgene #11150) with 1 µL NotI in 18 µL reaction buffer at 37 °C for 1 h.
Ligate the PCR product into the linearized vector with Ligation high Ver. 2 (Protocol 32, steps 1‑2).
Transform the ligation into DH5α competent cells (Protocol 5‑19, step 1‑1).

Isolate plasmid colonies, then linearize 1 µL of the purified pCAG‑GFP empty vector with 1 µL Esp3I (BsmBI) and 2 µL Tango buffer in 16 µL Milli‑Q water at 37 °C for 12–24 h (pre‑construction of pCAG‑miRNA‑GFP).
Optional dephosphorylation to prevent self‑ligation: treat vector with rapid alkaline phosphatase (Roche #4898141001) or equivalent.

steps.title: Extract RNA and make cDNA library
steps.instruction: Isolate total RNA from mouse medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and synthesize first‑strand cDNA using commercial kits.

substeps.instruction: Dissect ~30 mg of mPFC tissue from an anesthetized mouse and place in a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 600 µL Buffer RLT (RNeasy Mini Kit) and homogenize with a glass homogenizer.
Centrifuge lysate 3 min at >13 000 × g; transfer supernatant to a new tube.
Add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, mix, and load onto an RNeasy spin column (2 mL collection tube).
Wash column sequentially: 700 µL Buffer RW1 (30 s, >13 000 × g), then 500 µL Buffer RPE (30 s, >13 000 × g).
Place column in a fresh tube, add 40 µL RNase‑free water directly to the matrix, centrifuge 30 s (>13 000 × g) and discard flow‑through.
Aliquot RNA; store at –80 °C.
For reverse transcription, mix 1–2 µL RNA, 1 µL 6‑mer primer, 1 µL dNTP mix, bring to 10 µL with RNase‑free water; incubate 65 °C 5 min, chill on ice.
Add 4 µL 5× PrimeScript buffer, 0.5 µL RNase inhibitor, 1 µL PrimeScript RTase, 4.5 µL RNase‑free water; mix gently.
Incubate 30 °C 10 min, then 42 °C 60 min; inactivate at 95 °C 5 min.
Place cDNA on ice and store at –20 °C.
Critical: Use RNA from 3‑4‑week‑old male mice (or age/sex appropriate for target gene).
Store cDNA library at –80 °C for later rescue‑vector construction.

steps.title: Construct RNAi plasmids (KD, Scr, Control)
steps.instruction: Generate pCAG‑miRNA‑GFP (or ‑mOrange) plasmids for control, scramble, and knock‑down miRNAs using annealed oligos, ligation, and bacterial transformation.

substeps.instruction: Day 11 – Oligo annealing: Mix 5 µL top and 5 µL bottom oligos (designed in the RNAi design step) with 1 µL annealing buffer; heat 84 °C 4 min; cool on ice.
Elute 1 µL annealed oligos with 499 µL Milli‑Q water; keep remainder at –20 °C.
Ligate: combine 1 µL 500×‑eluted oligos, 0.5 µL pCAG‑GFP empty vector (no insert), 1.5 µL Ligation high Ver. 2; incubate 24‑27 °C 1 h.
Transform 50 µL DH5α competent cells with the ligation mix; keep on ice 30 min, heat‑shock 42 °C 30 s, ice 2 min, add 250 µL warm S.O.C., recover 37 °C 45‑60 min.
Plate on LB agar containing 0.01 % ampicillin (1.5 % agar, 2 % LB); incubate 12‑16 h at 37 °C.
Day 21 – Colony growth: Pick colonies with sterile tips, inoculate each tip into 3 mL 2 % LB + 300 µg/mL ampicillin (15 mL tube); grow 12‑16 h at 37 °C.
Day 31 – Glycerol stocks: Mix 1 mL of overnight culture with glycerol (final 15‑20 %); store at –80 °C.
Mini‑prep remaining culture using PureYield™ Plasmid Miniprep System (or equivalent); elute DNA, measure concentration (target 300‑450 ng/µL).
Confirm insertion by restriction digest (e.g., MscI) and/or Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Construct rescue vector (WT‑cDNA)
steps.instruction: Clone the full‑length cDNA of the target gene into a pCAG‑mOrange backbone, introduce miRNA‑resistant silent mutations, and verify the construct.

substeps.instruction: Search NCBI for the mouse (Mus musculus) cDNA of the target gene; retrieve the CDS.
Design forward and reverse primers (10 µM) to amplify the entire coding sequence; order commercially.
Prepare KOD‑plus Neo PCR master mix per reaction: 4 µL 10× buffer, 4 µL dNTPs, 2.4 µL MgSO₄, 2.4 µL primer mix (1.2 µL each), 1.6 µL cDNA library, 24.8 µL Milli‑Q water (total 40 µL).
Add 0.8 µL KOD‑plus Neo polymerase; vortex, spin down.
Add 40 µL master mix to a 200 µL PCR tube; run 2‑step PCR: 95 °C 10 min; 30 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 62 °C 30 s, 68 °C 30 s/kb; final 68 °C 7 min.
If target >3 kb, split into ≥2 fragments and clone separately.
Run 1.5 % agarose gel, excise correct bands, purify with Wizard® Genomic DNA Purification Kit.
Ligate purified PCR product (1 µL) with 1 µL linearized pCAG‑mOrange empty vector using 2 µL Ligation high Ver. 2; incubate 24‑27 °C 1 h.
Transform ligation into DH5α as described for RNAi plasmids; select on LB‑ampicillin plates.
Verify cDNA insertion by restriction digest (EcoRI, AgeI) and agarose electrophoresis.
Introduce silent mutations to disrupt miRNA binding: design QuikChange primers (replace 4‑6 nucleotides without altering codons).

QuikChange PCR (200 µL total): 1 µL forward primer (125 ng/µL), 1 µL reverse primer (125 ng/µL), 1 µL WT‑cDNA plasmid (50 ng/µL), 5 µL 10× buffer, 1 µL dNTP mix, 1.5 µL QuikSolution, 38.5 µL water; add 1 µL QuikChange Lightning enzyme; run 30 cycles: 95 °C 2 min, 95 °C 20 s, 60 °C 10 s, 68 °C 30 s/kb; final 68 °C 7 min.
Digest PCR product with 2 µL DpnI at 37 °C 5 min; transform into DH5α as above.
Confirm mutated rescue construct by sequencing.

steps.title: Validate KD efficiency in HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Transfect HEK293T cells with control, scramble, KD, and rescue plasmids, then assess GFP/mOrange expression and target knock‑down by immunocytochemistry.

substeps.instruction: Day 1 – Cell seeding: Plate HEK293T cells to reach ~50 % confluence in a 100 mm dish.
Detach with 500 µL trypsin in 3 mL HBSS; incubate 3‑5 min at 37 °C, 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂.
Neutralize with 7 mL HBSS, collect, centrifuge 110 × g 3 min (<20 °C), resuspend in 12 mL DMEM.
Dispense 0.5 mL suspension per well of a 24‑well plate.
Day 2 – Transfection setup (6 h before transfection): Prepare four 1.5 mL tubes with 50 µL OPTI‑MEM per well (total 300 µL for 6‑well).

Add plasmid mixes (final per well): 0.2 µg WT‑cDNA + 0.3 µg GFP (control); 0.2 µg WT‑cDNA + 0.3 µg KD‑miRNA; 0.2 µg WT‑cDNA + 0.3 µg Scr‑miRNA; 0.2 µg cDNA‑rescue + 0.3 µg KD‑miRNA. Adjust volumes to 0.5 µg total DNA per well.
Add 1.5 µL X‑tremeGene™ HP to each tube, incubate 15 min at 24‑27 °C.
Add transfection mix to corresponding wells; repeat transfection after 6 h (total two transfections).
Day 3 – Fixation: Replace medium with 4 % PFA, incubate 10 min at 24‑27 °C; wash 3× PBS.
Permeabilize with 300 µL PBS + 0.1 % Triton X‑100 for 10 min (24‑27 °C).
Block with 30 µL donkey serum for 30 min (24‑27 °C).
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in PBS: anti‑GFP 1:1000, anti‑RFP (mOrange) 1:300.
Day 4 – Secondary staining: Wash 3× PBS, incubate 1 h at 24‑27 °C with secondary antibodies (1:400 in PBS).
Wash, then image on a confocal microscope (capture 5‑6 fields per well).

steps.title: In utero electroporation of plasmids
steps.instruction: Inject plasmid DNA into embryonic mouse lateral ventricles at E14.5 and deliver electric pulses to target medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) pyramidal neurons.

substeps.instruction: Pull injection pipettes (1.5 mm OD × 0.86 mm ID × 100 mm) using a Flaming/Brown puller: Step 1 HEAT = 602, PULL = 35, VEL = 200, TIME = 250; Step 2 HEAT = 604, PULL = 0, VEL = 200, TIME = 250. Tip diameter ≈0.1‑0.2 mm.
Anesthetize a pregnant ICR mouse (E14.5 embryos are optimal).
Expose the uterine horns via a 3‑5 cm abdominal incision; keep embryos moist with autoclaved PBS.
Using a glass capillary, inject 2‑3 µL DNA solution (1‑3 µg/µL in PBS; total 2‑9 µg per embryo) into each lateral ventricle (0.75‑1.0 mm anterior to lambda, 0.5 mm lateral to sagittal suture).
Place bipolar forceps electrodes flanking the mPFC (negative pole over injected hemisphere).
Deliver 5 pulses: 35 V, 50 ms duration, 950 ms interval.
Suture the abdominal wall, administer analgesic, and allow dam to recover.
Optional: For sparse opsin expression, co‑inject 1‑2 µg/µL pCAG‑DIO‑Chronos‑GFP plus 0.5‑1 ng/µL pCAG‑Cre with 1‑2 µg/µL pCAG‑KD‑miRNA‑mOrange.
Post‑natal verification: 1‑3 days after birth, examine pups through the skull with green/red light glasses; retain 6‑7 pups with strong fluorescence for further experiments.

steps.title: Prepare acute brain slices
steps.instruction: Section the mPFC of post‑natal mice (P16‑25 preferred) in chilled cutting solution and recover slices for electrophysiology.

substeps.instruction: Prepare cutting solution (either potassium‑gluconate‑based for >P60 or choline‑Cl‑based for younger mice) and chill on ice 30 min‑1 h while bubbling 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂.
Anesthetize mouse with CO₂ (or isoflurane) and decapitate; remove brain within <1 min.
Place brain in ice‑cold cutting solution for ~3 min.
Trim posterior brain to expose +1.0‑+2.0 mm anterior to bregma.
Mount brain in vibratome chamber (VT1200, Leica) and cut 4‑5 coronal slices containing mPFC at 250‑300 µm thickness (cortex ≈ 300 µm, cerebrum ≈ 250 µm).
Transfer slices to a holding chamber with ACSF at 24‑27 °C for 30‑60 min (or water bath at 37 °C as alternative).

steps.title: Set up patch‑clamp recording
steps.instruction: Pull borosilicate patch pipettes, fill with internal solution, and position on target pyramidal neurons in the slice.

substeps.instruction: Pull pipettes from 1.5 mm OD × 1.17 mm ID × 100 mm glass (Harvard Apparatus #30‑0062) using a Sutter P‑97 puller: Step 1 HEAT = 572, PULL = 0, VEL = 81, TIME = 250; Step 2 HEAT = 570, PULL = 0, VEL = 60, TIME = 250. Aim for 2.4‑5 MΩ resistance.
Mount slice in recording chamber on DIC microscope; maintain bath temperature at 30‑32 °C.
Identify layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons by morphology and/or GFP/mOrange fluorescence.
Approach cell with positive pressure; release pressure to form giga‑ohm seal; gradually change holding potential from 0 mV to –70 mV.
Break into whole‑cell configuration using gentle suction or “zap” pulse.

steps.title: Record synaptic currents
steps.instruction: Measure spontaneous, miniature, and evoked synaptic events under defined pharmacological conditions.

substeps.instruction: Set amplifier filter to 2.9 kHz; ensure series resistance <20 MΩ (preferably <10 MΩ).
Record spontaneous EPSCs at –70 mV in 0.1 mM picrotoxin.
Record spontaneous IPSCs at –70 mV in 10 µM NBQX + 50 µM D‑AP5.
For miniature events, add 0.5 µM TTX plus the respective blockers (0.1 mM picrotoxin for mEPSCs; 10 µM NBQX + 50 µM D‑AP5 for mIPSCs).
Evoked AMPAR‑EPSCs: hold –70 mV, perfuse 0.1 mM picrotoxin + 50 µM D‑AP5.
Evoked NMDAR‑EPSCs: hold –70 mV, perfuse 0.5 µM TTX + 10 µM NBQX, stimulate at +40 mV.
Evoked IPSCs: hold –70 mV, perfuse 10 µM NBQX + 50 µM D‑AP5, stimulate at 0 mV.
If spontaneous/miniature responses are abnormal, proceed to evoked recordings using a bipolar tungsten stimulating electrode placed 50‑100 µm from the patched cell.
Deliver paired‑pulse electrical stimuli (0.1 ms) at inter‑stimulus intervals 20, 50, 100, 500 ms; optionally 1 s.
For optogenetic stimulation, use 465‑nm LED (LEX2‑LZ4‑B) at 4 mW/mm², pulse 2‑10 ms; adjust intensity so first EPSC amplitude ≈50‑100 pA.

steps.title: Analyze spine morphology
steps.instruction: Immunostain slices for GFP and mOrange, acquire high‑resolution confocal images, and quantify dendritic spine parameters.

substeps.instruction: Fix slices (if not already) and block with donkey serum.
Incubate with primary antibodies against GFP and RFP (mOrange) as needed.
Apply appropriate fluorescent secondary antibodies; wash thoroughly.
Image using a confocal microscope with 60× oil immersion, digital zoom 2.0, 0.48 µm z‑step, 1024 × 1024 px resolution.
Capture 5‑6 images per neuron; aim for 20‑30 neurons per condition.

Analyze spines with Neurolucida 360 using criteria: outer range 2.5 µm, min height 0.3 µm, detector 50 %, min voxels 10, head‑to‑neck ratio ≥ 1.1, length‑to‑head ratio ≥ 2.5, mushroom head size ≥ 0.35 µm, filopodium length ≤ 3 µm.
Count spine number and measure head width; compute averages.

steps.title: Process electrophysiology data
steps.instruction: Analyze recorded traces to obtain input‑output curves, paired‑pulse ratios, and excitation/inhibition balance, then perform statistical testing.

substeps.instruction: Use PATCHMASTER/FITMASTER (HEKA) to extract amplitudes and frequencies of spontaneous, miniature, and evoked events.
For PPR, average 5‑10 traces per inter‑stimulus interval; calculate ratio of second to first EPSC.
For I/E balance, record evoked EPSC at –40 mV (50 µM D‑AP5), confirm NBQX block; then record evoked IPSC at 0 mV, confirm picrotoxin block.
Correct liquid junction potential based on internal and ACSF compositions.
Set detection thresholds in Mini Analysis (≥5 pA amplitude, rise time ≤3 ms).
Statistical analysis: for two‑group comparisons use Student’s t‑test or Mann‑Whitney U (based on normality); for multiple groups use two‑way ANOVA. Perform analyses in EZR or Prism.
